key_insight: Simple MLPs pretrained on low-resolution spectra (or their embeddings) can be effectively fine-tuned to estimate stellar parameters from moderate-resolution spectra (LAMOST → DESI), enabling cross-survey generalization with far fewer labeled target examples.
problem_solved: Addresses the domain-shift challenge in stellar spectral analysis: how to transfer models trained on abundant low-resolution survey data to new moderate-resolution surveys without large labeled datasets for the target instrument.
method: Pretrain small neural networks (MLPs) on LAMOST low-resolution spectra or on fixed embeddings derived from those spectra.
Transfer learned weights to DESI moderate-resolution spectra and fine-tune with a limited number of labeled DESI examples (optionally freezing early layers or using lightweight adapters).
Evaluate parameter recovery (e.g., Teff, log g, [Fe/H]) against baselines (training from scratch on DESI) to quantify sample efficiency and generalization.
impact: Demonstrates that lightweight architectures plus transfer learning and embedding-based pretraining can overcome survey domain gaps, cutting labeling needs and accelerating deployment of stellar-parameter models for new spectroscopic surveys.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LAMOST spectra → pretrain MLP / embeddings → transfer & fine-tune → DESI predictions
Bar/line chart: performance vs. number of DESI labels comparing scratch training, spectrum-pretrained, and embedding-pretrained models
Embedding projection (t-SNE/UMAP): LAMOST vs DESI feature overlap before and after fine-tuning
Spectral overlay icon: example low-res vs moderate-res spectrum with predicted parameter annotations
paper_title: Generalization from Low- to Moderate-Resolution Spectra with Neural Networks for Stellar Parameter Estimation: A Case Study with DESI
paper_authors: Xiaosheng Zhao, Yuan-Sen Ting, Rosemary F. G. Wyse, Alexander S. Szalay, Yang Huang
